# iliad-063 (Iliad 10.482–579) — reviewer, pass 1

`t` untouched (checked: units' `t` joined = packet lines 482–579; `ln`, `p`, `mark`, line counts of `t`/`l`, and “ ” balance all verified by script). Edits made to `units.json` by script; `new-renderings.md` fixed where a rendering changed.

## Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. 547 · `i` (+ `n`, new-renderings) · major · `i` said "Strikingly like the rays of the sun", departing from the house table, which renders αἰνῶς "dreadfully" in both layers, including with ἔοικεν (3.158 "dreadfully … is like"; also 9.244, 8.397). The drafter's reason (plain intensifier) is not a licence to vary a table word. · `i` now "Dreadfully like the rays of the sun."; note's first sentence now says αἰνῶς is an intensifier ("awfully like" in English idiom) and that the English keeps "dreadfully"; new-renderings row rewritten (l = i).
2. 555 · `n` · major · note said the address ὦ Νέστορ Νηληϊάδη … "also opens Odysseus' speech at 10.87". The speech at 10.87 (iliad-058, mark "Agamemnon answers") is Agamemnon's. · "Odysseus'" → "Agamemnon's".
3. 555 · `n` · minor · note called the particle in ἐπεὶ ἢ πολὺ "ἦ", but the line prints ἢ. · now "the particle printed ἢ read as ἦ 'truly'".
4. 572 · `n` · moderate · ἐσβάντες was labelled the aorist participle of ἐμβαίνω; it is from εἰσβαίνω/ἐσβαίνω ("step into"; ἐμβαίνω would give ἐμβάντες). · corrected.
5. 572 · `n` · minor · scansion sentence leaked pipeline language ("The scanner flagged this line") and said only "the short syllable in the fourth foot". Hand scan: syllables αὐ-τοὶ | δ'ἱ-δρῶ | πολ-λὸν | ἀ-πε-νί | ζον-το-θα | λάσ-σῃ (14 syllables, so two dactyls; the only place for them is feet 4 and 5; foot 4 needs a long first syllable, but ἀ- of ἀπενίζοντο is short; ἱ- of ἱδρῶ is also long, by position before δρ, which is ordinary). The irregularity is real. · sentence now: "The line is metrically irregular as transmitted: it scans only if the first syllable of ἀπενίζοντο, which opens the fourth foot, is read long (metrical lengthening)."
6. 531 · `i` (+ `n`, new-renderings) · minor · `i` "for that was where their spirit wanted to go" drops φίλον and invents "wanted"; the house row for φίλον ἔπλετο θυμῷ has `i` "pleased". · `i` now "for it pleased their spirit to go that way"; note says the English gives "was dear to the spirit" as "it pleased the spirit"; `l` kept (see refused 1).
7. 535 · `l` (+ `n`, new-renderings) · minor · μ' rendered twice in `l` ("around me … my ears"). · `l` now "Of horses swift-footed the thud around strikes my ears."; note says the pronoun is rendered once, in "my ears".
8. 561 · `n` · moderate · note said Odysseus "counts the scout as the thirteenth victim", presenting two incompatible counts (495: king thirteenth; 559–561: king and twelve, then scout thirteenth) as one coherent tally. · now says plainly that 495 called the king the thirteenth, the two counts do not agree, and the Greek is rendered as it stands. (`i` "thirteenth" kept in both places so the reader sees the same number as the Greek.)
9. 561 · `l` · minor · `l` began "and as the thirteenth …" though the Greek has no conjunction (asyndeton after the full stop at 560); new-renderings already had it without "and". · "and" dropped from `l`; `i` keeps "and" as English connective, like 517.
10. 567 · `l` · minor · `l` "to the horses' manger" for φάτνῃ ἐφ' ἱππείῃ (ἐπί + dative, "at/on"), while `i` and the new-renderings row say "at". · `l` → "at the horses' manger"; new-renderings row updated.
11. 567 · `n` · minor · note quoted ἱμᾶσιν; the line has ἱμᾶσι. · quoted as printed.
12. 483 (second unit) · `n` · minor · "the sleeping Thracians of 474": the Thracians are described asleep at 471 (474 is Rhesus). · "of 471".
13. 498 · `n` · minor · "ὁ before τλήμων"; the line prints ὃ. · "ὃ".

Counts: major 2, moderate 2, minor 9 (13 changes in 11 units).

## Findings considered and refused

1. 531 · `l` "their spirit": the Greek has no pronoun, but English needs one; the note already says the Greek does not say whose heart. Kept.
2. 531 · τῇ as "thither" and ἔπλετο: grammar of note is true (adverbial dative of the article, local); no cross-reference to fix. Kept.
3. 535 · whether μ' is με or μοι: both are possible with βάλλει (acc. of person + acc. of part, or dat. of interest); the note states both and the English is the same. No change beyond item 7.
4. 546 · `i` turns the indirect question (ὅππως … ἦ τίς) into a direct one while `l` keeps the Greek's full stop. Kept: the published prefix of this speech-opening line ends in a colon ("… great glory of the Achaeans:"), so a direct question follows naturally, and the note already labels the construction indirect. (The archive prints a stop, not a Greek question mark, after ἀντιβολήσας; not my business at review, and `t` is not touched.)
5. 551 / 546 · ὔμμ' / σφωε each stand once in the Greek but are rendered twice in `l` ("having met you … to you"): they are shared by the participle and the main verb (apo koinou); English cannot do otherwise. Note labels (dative ὔμμι, dual accusative σφωε) are true. Kept.
6. 513 · note "there is no chariot, so he gets up on a horse": consistent with the part (504–505 the chariot is left behind). Kept.
7. 548–549 · `i` "old though I am, and a warrior": the Greek γέρων περ ἐὼν πολεμιστής allows this; no change.
8. 544 · published prefix check: `l`/`i` first line equals iliad-057's (9.673). OK.
9. 512, 530, 533 (first line), 552 (first half-line), 554, 555 (first line), 576, 534, 540, 542: repeated lines compared with the published Iliad/Odyssey units; wording agrees (576 with odyssey-014; 534 and 533's second line with odyssey-015; 540 with odyssey-077; 542 with odyssey-096; 552 with iliad-043; 530 with iliad-030/-034/-046).
10. 557 · "the subject of εἰσιν is the gods": a reading, not a certainty, but the only plural antecedent that gives sense; note states it plainly and the `i` says "the gods". Kept.
11. 563 / 561 · `l` "noble ones" / `i` "noble" (ἀγαυοί) and all other epithets (γλαυκῶπις, ἀργυρότοξος, πολύμητις, δῖος, κρατερός, Γερήνιος ἱππότα, πολύαινος, μεγάθυμος, νεφεληγερέτα, αἰγιόχοιο, μώνυχες, ὠκύποδες, καλλίτριχες, ποικίλος, ἀργαλέος, μέρμερα, ἀεικής, εὔτυκτος, κλισίη, μελιηδής, Διῒ φίλος, τλήμων, βουληφόρος, ἀνεψιός, κρητήρ, θοός): checked against the tables; all agree.
12. 535 / 538 αἰνῶς at 538 ("dreadfully" in both layers) agrees with the table's 9.244 row. OK.
13. 518–519 · `i` of 519 ends on a comma and runs into 522: sentence-unit split follows the Greek stops (· at 518, full stop at 522 is the next unit's); fine.

# Pass 2 (gloss) — reviewer

Scope: every `gloss.json` entry (123 novel forms plus 19 `__broaden__` entries) checked against the line(s) where the form stands, with `units.json` `l`/`i`/`n`; structure checked by script (keys = `novel-forms.json` exactly; no digits-as-line-numbers, no "here", no ASCII apostrophe, every novel entry under 230 characters; every `__broaden__` entry begins with the whole old entry from `known-forms.json` plus ` · `). Known forms not in `__broaden__` were re-read against their lines (all 338 of them): no further broadening needed. `gloss.json` and `units.json` edited by script; `t` untouched.

## Changes (form · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. ὔμμ (ὔμμ’) · moderate · entry gave only the dative ὔμμι, but the elision cannot decide between ὔμμι and ὔμμε (accusative, Attic ὑμᾶς; the ι of a Homeric dative is often held not to elide, and ἀντιάω may take an accusative of the person met) · both readings now given, joined by ` · `, with "the elision does not tell which".
2. 551 note · moderate · the unit note asserted "the elided dative of ὔμμι" · note now says ὔμμ’ is ὔμμι (dative) or ὔμμε (accusative), the elision does not decide, as accusative the object of ἀντιάσαντα, as dative with δόμεναι, sense "you" either way (`l`/`i` unchanged and true of both).
3. ἐγείρῃσιν (511 note) · moderate · note said "-ῃσιν for -ωσι"; -ωσι is the 3 pl. subjunctive ending, the subject here is singular (θεὸς ἄλλος), and the Attic form is -ῃ · note now "-ῃσιν for -ῃ".
4. ἐγείρῃσιν (gloss) · minor · quoted gloss "lest (he) rouse" invents a pronoun, while the subject is the noun θεὸς ἄλλος · now "lest … rouse"; the parse (subj. 3 sg., pres. or aor., after μή of fear) is true.
5. διοπτῆρα · minor · entry and note called it "in apposition" to σκοπόν; with ἔμμεναι (…τὸν… διοπτῆρα… ἔμμεναι) it is the predicate accusative of the infinitive, "to be a spy" · entry now "predicate accusative with ἔμμεναι"; 561 note reworded the same way.
6. κύντατον · minor · entry's quoted gloss "the boldest (deed)" disagrees with the unit's `i` ("most shameless") and its own head-gloss · now "the most shameless (deed)".
7. τρισκαιδέκατον · minor · entry pinned to one line ("agreeing with τόν"); the form stands twice, once with τόν and once before a noun (σκοπόν) · now "agreeing with the object (τόν or a noun with it): ’the thirteenth’".
8. ἀσημάντοισιν · minor · entry stated "unshepherded, without a keeper" as the meaning and a derivation from σημαίνω "give orders", while the unit note says the literal sense is "unmarked, without a sign" and "unguarded" is only the usual explanation, exact sense not certain · entry now "unmarked, without a sign (ἀ- + σημαίνω ’mark’); traditionally ’unguarded, with no herdsman’, exact sense not certain".
9. ἔπεφνεν · minor · "root aorist ἔπεφνον with reduplicated stem" is self-contradictory (a reduplicated aorist is not a root aorist) · now "ἔπεφνον is a reduplicated aorist (stem πε-φν-) used as aorist of θείνω, with no present in use".
10. ἤειρεν · minor · entry said "aor." only; ἤειρε(ν) is identical in the 3 sg. of aorist and imperfect (and the neighbours λύε, ἐξήλαυνεν are imperfects) · now "aor. (or impf.)".
11. ἐξερέεινε · minor · "(= Attic ἐξηρώτα)" names a different verb as if it were the Attic form · now "(Attic ἐξερωτάω ’ask out’)" as the Attic counterpart.
12. πλείου · minor (the glosser's doubt, parse upheld) · πλείου is gen. sg. masc. of πλεῖος "full" agreeing with κρητῆρος ("from a full bowl"), not a comparative; the parse was right, but the Homeric form had no Attic equivalent named · lemma now "πλεῖος (Attic πλέως)", "masc. gen. sg. (Attic πλέω)".
13. αἴγεσιν · minor · "uncontracted ending -εσιν" is not the right description (it is the epic dative-plural ending) and αἴξ is not feminine only · now "masc./fem. dat. pl., epic -εσιν (Attic αἰξί)".
14. `__broaden__` λίπ · minor · new reading said "neut. acc. sg. of λίπα used as adv.", which explains λίπα by itself · now "λίπα — richly, sleekly (adv.), elided (λίπ’ = λίπα)".

Counts: major 0, moderate 3 (items 1–3), minor 11 (items 4–14); 14 changes (12 in `gloss.json`, 3 notes in `units.json`; item 5 touches both).

## Findings considered and refused

1. πρυμνῇ (glosser's doubt) · the accent settles it: πρυμνῇ (perispomenon) is the dative of the adjective πρυμνός agreeing with νηΐ; the noun πρύμνῃ would be paroxytone. Entry already says so. Kept.
2. ἀντιάσαντα (doubt) · aor. part. act. masc. acc. sg. of ἀντιάω, agreeing with θεόν; nothing wrong. Kept (the case of its object is dealt with under ὔμμ’).
3. ἔκταν (doubt) · 3 pl. (subject: the two heroes), root aorist, Attic ἔκτειναν; true. Kept.
4. ἀήθεσσον · the verb is ἀηθέω in the entry, and LSJ may list the -σσ- form under ἀηθέσσω; I cannot settle the headword without the book, and the parse (impf. 3 pl., unaugmented, + gen.) is true of the line. Kept.
5. ψεύσομαι · could also be a short-vowel aorist subjunctive; the unit note and the known entry for ἐρέω both say future, the sense is the same ("shall I … ?"). Kept.
6. τίς (broaden, "some", after ἦ) · the printed accent invites the interrogative "what god?", which the old entry already covers; the unit's `l`/`i` take it as indefinite ("some god"), so the added reading is true of the use. Kept.
7. μ’ at 544 (εἴπ’ ἄγε μ’) and 535 · the old entry covers acc. "me", and the dative alternative is already given; the unit note states both. No broadening.
8. καταδύντες "aor. 2 part." and a plural participle with the dual λάβετον · true and usual in Homer; no change.
9. ἕρδοι "(= Attic ῥέζω)" · ῥέζω is the poetic Attic-form name the Odyssey glossary also uses; kept.
10. All other novel entries (case, number, tense, mood, voice, gender, Attic equivalent, article-forms, homographs) and the other 18 `__broaden__` entries (αὐτῶν, βάλλει, κακὸν, κατεδύσετο, κοτέων, λόφον, μηδὲ, μῆτιν, πολλὸν, πουλὺν, τάφροιο, τρώεσσ, τόξῳ, ἐσθλόν, ἔλθῃς, ἢ, ὅπως, τίς) checked against their lines: true of the use, old entry whole, new reading added with ` · `. Kept.
